prompt:
This TOML loads fine with stdlib tomllib, but tomlkit.parse fails on it:

[[fruit]]
apple.color = "red"

[potato]

[fruit.apple.texture]
smooth = true

from tomlkit import parse
parse(open("fruit.toml").read())

ParseError: Key "fruit" already exists. at line 7 col 0

If I move [potato] to the end of the file, it parses. [fruit.apple.texture] extends the last [[fruit]] element, which is valid TOML even with another table in between. I expected doc["fruit"][0]["apple"]["color"] == "red", doc["fruit"][0]["apple"]["texture"]["smooth"] is True, and doc["potato"] == {}.
test_patch:
diff --git a/tests/test_toml_document.py b/tests/test_toml_document.py
index 1cdfb9c..1b0508b 100644
--- a/tests/test_toml_document.py
+++ b/tests/test_toml_document.py
@@ -239,6 +239,25 @@ name = "Test 1"
     assert doc["foo"]["bar"]["tests"][0]["name"] == "Test 1"
 
 
+def test_subtable_of_aot_element_after_other_table() -> None:
+    # A sub-table header that extends the last element of an array of tables
+    # is valid even when an unrelated table appears in between (issue #261).
+    content = """[[fruit]]
+apple.color = "red"
+
+[potato]
+
+[fruit.apple.texture]
+smooth = true
+"""
+
+    doc = parse(content)
+
+    assert doc["fruit"][0]["apple"]["color"] == "red"
+    assert doc["fruit"][0]["apple"]["texture"]["smooth"] is True
+    assert doc["potato"] == {}

prompt_original:
Fix ParseError when a sub-table extends an array of tables out of order (#498)

* Fix ParseError when a sub-table extends the last array-of-tables element after an unrelated table

When a sub-table header such as [fruit.apple.texture] follows the array
[[fruit]] with an unrelated table in between, the parser rebuilds it as a
fresh super table named "fruit" and tries to append it to the document,
colliding with the existing array of tables and raising

    ParseError: Key "fruit" already exists.

even though the document is valid TOML 1.0.0. The contiguous form (no
intervening table) already worked because the sub-table is consumed while
the array element is still being parsed.

A sub-table header that refers to an existing array of tables extends the
array's last element, regardless of any tables defined in between, so merge
its contents into that element instead of treating it as a redefinition.
Defining a non-super table with the same name as an array (e.g. [fruit]
after [[fruit]]) is still a genuine conflict and continues to raise.

Fixes #261

* Document the out-of-order array-of-tables round-trip limitation
